source_meta._title: /execute running chat related commands logs "Received chat packet without valid signature" warning

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition client running 1.19 Pre-release 1 in a single-player world hosted by the integrated server. Use a fresh Creative-mode Superflat world with commands allowed and difficulty set to Normal or another non-Peaceful difficulty. The active client log must be accessible through the instance's logs/latest.log file or an equivalent client-output monitor.
preconditions: Launch the affected version stated in the report: Minecraft Java Edition 1.19 Pre-release 1.
Use an unmodified client without mods that replace or intercept chat, commands, or logging.
Commands must be permitted in the test world. For the proposed Creative-world setup, enable Allow Cheats when creating the world.
Do not use Peaceful difficulty, because the summoned creeper can be removed immediately on that difficulty.
Use the in-game chat screen for the reported /execute command. Do not substitute a command block, function, server console, or launcher console.
Ensure the client-side log for the active game instance can be read. In a standard instance this is the logs/latest.log file inside that instance's game directory.
If controls have been rebound, use the control assigned to Open Chat instead of the default T key.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation that uses Minecraft Java Edition 1.19 Pre-release 1, then launch that installation.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is open and its version label identifies 1.19 Pre-release 1.

steps.action: From the title screen, select Singleplayer, then select Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Configure the new world for Game Mode: Creative, set Allow Cheats to ON, select the Superflat world type under the additional world options, and leave or set the difficulty to Normal. Then create the world.
steps.success_cue: World generation begins with Creative mode, commands enabled, a Superflat world type, and a non-Peaceful difficulty.

steps.action: Wait for the player to enter the world. Do not continue until the flat terrain around the player has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player can move normally in a fully rendered portion of the Superflat world.

steps.action: Open the active instance's client log file, normally logs/latest.log, in a monitor that can display newly appended lines. Position the monitor at the current end of the file, but do not evaluate the bug outcome yet. Keep Minecraft focused for the following game actions.
steps.success_cue: The client log monitor is attached to the active game's log and is positioned after the existing entries.

steps.action: In Minecraft, press the default Open Chat key to open the in-game chat screen.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is visible and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Type the following command exactly into the chat input. Include the leading slash, but do not submit it until the complete command is present.
steps.success_cue: The complete summon command is visible in the chat input field with no extra characters.

steps.action: Press Enter once to execute the summon command.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted and one creeper is visible or the command feedback confirms that a Creeper was summoned near the player.

steps.action: Press the default Open Chat key again. Perform this while the summoned creeper is still present and loaded in the world.
steps.success_cue: The in-game chat input field is open while the summoned creeper remains loaded.

steps.action: Type the report's command exactly into the chat input. Preserve its capitalization and spacing, include the leading slash, and do not add a slash before the say subcommand.
steps.success_cue: The complete command /execute as @e[type=creeper] run say Hi is visible in the chat input field and has not yet been submitted.

steps.action: Press Enter once to submit the /execute command from the in-game chat screen. Do not run it again; immediately hand control to the observation subsystem after this single execution.
steps.success_cue: The chat screen closes, the command has executed as the loaded creeper, and an in-game say message containing Hi is produced by the creeper.

stor.handoff_condition: The exact command /execute as @e[type=creeper] run say Hi has just been submitted once from the in-game chat screen while the summoned creeper is loaded, and the client log monitor is positioned to inspect entries appended by that execution. Begin client-log observation now.
uncertainties: The report does not state whether the original test used single-player or a dedicated server. This plan uses a single-player integrated server because it is the simplest setup that preserves execution from the client chat screen and access to the client log.

The report does not specify the game mode, world type, difficulty, or exact method used to summon the creeper. Creative mode, Superflat terrain, Normal difficulty, and /summon creeper ~2 ~ ~ are deterministic operational choices rather than report requirements.

The report does not identify an operating system, launcher configuration, or absolute log path. The active instance's logs/latest.log file should be used; its parent game directory may differ for custom installations.

The externally verified summon command supplies the omitted operational detail for report step 1. The report's /execute command is preserved exactly and has not been modernized or otherwise rewritten.

stor.recommended_version: Minecraft Java Edition 1.19 release (preferred deterministic affected version; the report also lists snapshot 22w24a). Do not create the test world in a later version.
stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition client running a singleplayer world through the integrated server, with cheats enabled. The report specifies no world seed, game mode, difficulty, resource pack, datapack, server, or additional player.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher can start an installation using the Java Edition 1.19 release.
A keyboard and mouse are available; default controls are assumed below, but equivalent rebound controls may be used.
The complete command from the report is available to paste as one line.
When entering the command, preserve the single backslash followed by lowercase n in `Players:\n`; do not replace it with a literal line break and do not add a second backslash.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select or create an installation that uses the exact Java Edition 1.19 release, then start the game with that installation.
steps.success_cue: The main menu is open and the lower-left version label identifies the running game as Minecraft 1.19.

steps.action: From the main menu, select `Singleplayer`, then select `Create New World`.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Open `More World Options...` and toggle `Allow Cheats` until it reads `Allow Cheats: ON`. The report does not require a particular seed, game mode, or other world setting, so leave those settings unchanged.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows that cheats are enabled.

steps.action: Select `Create New World` and wait for world generation and loading to finish. Do not continue while a loading screen is visible.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the singleplayer world, surrounding terrain has rendered, and normal movement and input are responsive.

steps.action: Press `T` to open in-game chat. Paste the report command into the chat input as one uninterrupted line. Include the leading `/`, preserve all quotation marks and backslashes exactly, and press `Enter` once to execute it.
steps.success_cue: The chat overlay closes after command submission and a new `Click me!` text component is visible in the chat area. No command-syntax error is shown.

steps.action: Press `T` again to open the full chat interface. Locate the `Click me!` line created by the preceding command; if necessary, use the chat history area rather than typing anything new.
steps.success_cue: The chat interface is open, the mouse pointer is available, and the `Click me!` text component is visible and unobstructed.

steps.action: Move the mouse pointer directly over the visible `Click me!` text component and left-click it exactly once. Do not click elsewhere, enter another command, or repeat the click before handing control to the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: A single left-click has just been issued on the `Click me!` chat component; no further reproduction input has been performed.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just left-clicked the `Click me!` text component once in the chat interface of the Minecraft Java Edition 1.19 singleplayer world. Begin observation immediately without providing further input.
uncertainties: The report lists both Java Edition 1.19 and snapshot 22w24a as affected but does not designate one as the preferred test version; this plan selects the stable 1.19 release.
The report does not specify a game mode, seed, difficulty, world type, or customized controls; none are treated as required.
The report says to `press` the text but does not explicitly name the mouse button; left-click is used as the standard activation input for a chat click event.
No external verification was needed because the supplied report includes the exact affected versions, environment requirement, command, action order, and trigger.

source_meta._title: Debug messages aren't prefixed with gray color indicators

stor.recommended_version: Minecraft Java Edition 1.19.1 Pre-release 6 (launcher version 1.19.1-pre6), the exact affected version named in the report
stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition client in a single-player world using the integrated server. Use a keyboard that can send the F3+B debug-key combination. Creative mode and enabled cheats are selected as practical setup choices so the supplied command can be executed without additional permission configuration.
preconditions: Install or make available Minecraft Java Edition 1.19.1 Pre-release 6 in the Minecraft Launcher.
Use an unmodified client unless the supplied test environment specifically requires otherwise.
Ensure chat is not hidden, because both the command-feedback message and the debug message must be available in chat history.
Ensure cheats are enabled or the player otherwise has permission to execute /tag.
Start with a player that does not already have the tag named test; a newly created world and player satisfy this condition.
Do not clear chat between executing the command and invoking the debug function.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select an installation that uses Minecraft Java Edition 1.19.1 Pre-release 6, and launch the game. Do not substitute 1.19.1 Release Candidate 2 or a later version.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is open and identifies the running version as 1.19.1 Pre-release 6.

steps.action: From the title screen, open the single-player world-creation screen by selecting Singleplayer and then Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is visible.

steps.action: Set Game Mode to Creative. Open More World Options and confirm that Allow Cheats is set to ON. No particular world seed or world-generation setting is required by the report.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; More World Options... -> Allow Cheats: ON
steps.success_cue: The world is configured for Creative mode and commands are permitted.

steps.action: Select Create New World and wait for world generation and loading to finish.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the world, surrounding terrain has rendered, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Confirm that chat messages are visible. If chat is hidden, open the pause menu and change the chat visibility through Options, Chat Settings, Chat until it reads Shown; then return to the world.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options... -> Chat Settings... -> Chat: Shown -> Done -> Done -> Back to Game
steps.success_cue: Gameplay is active again and chat visibility is set to Shown.

steps.action: Press the Open Chat control, whose default key is T, so that an in-game command can be entered.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and has keyboard focus.

steps.action: Enter the report's command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter to execute it as the current player.
steps.success_cue: The chat input closes and a command-feedback line reporting the tag operation is displayed in the chat area.

steps.action: Allow the command-feedback line to finish rendering, and leave it in chat history as the comparison system-message entry. Ensure normal gameplay has keyboard focus before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The tag command's feedback line is retained in chat history and no menu or text-entry field is open.

steps.action: Invoke the hitbox debug function by holding F3, pressing B once, and then releasing the keys. On a keyboard where the function row controls media features, also hold the hardware Fn key as necessary. Do not repeatedly toggle the function.
steps.exact_input: F3+B (or Fn+F3+B when required by the keyboard)
steps.success_cue: A hitbox-debug status message has been emitted to chat, and the hitbox display state has toggled once.

steps.action: Immediately press T to open the expanded chat history so that both the earlier command-feedback line and the newly emitted debug-status line are visible for the observation subsystem. Do not enter or send any additional text.
steps.success_cue: The expanded chat interface is open and contains both the tag-command feedback entry and the F3+B debug-status entry.

stor.handoff_condition: The F3+B debug function has just been toggled once, and the expanded chat history is open with both the prior /tag command-feedback entry and the resulting debug-status entry available for inspection. Hand control to the observation subsystem before closing or clearing chat.
uncertainties: The report does not specify single-player versus multiplayer, game mode, world seed, operating system, or keyboard model. A fresh Creative single-player world with cheats enabled is the simplest deterministic setup that preserves the reported actions.
The report permits any debug function and gives F3+B as its example. This plan uses F3+B exactly to avoid selecting an unsupported alternative.
Whether a hardware Fn modifier is required depends on the keyboard and operating-system configuration; Fn is not part of Minecraft's logical debug-key combination.

The exact wording of the tag command feedback and hitbox debug message is not prescribed as a setup requirement, so the plan only requires that the corresponding entries be emitted and retained for inspection.

source_meta._title: Screenshot messages aren't prefixed with gray color indicators

stor.recommended_version: Minecraft Java Edition 1.19.1 Pre-release 6 (the affected version; do not use 1.19.1 Release Candidate 2, which the report lists as the fix version)
stor.environment: A single-player Minecraft Java Edition world running 1.19.1 Pre-release 6, with commands permitted and chat visible. A new Creative-mode world is the simplest practical setup because commands are enabled automatically; the report does not require a particular game mode, seed, coordinates, or server configuration.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected version, Minecraft Java Edition 1.19.1 Pre-release 6.

Use a world in which the player can execute commands. For the simplest deterministic setup, create a new single-player world in Creative mode; alternatively, use any world with cheats enabled or sufficient command permission.
Ensure chat messages are visible. If necessary, open Esc -> Options -> Chat Settings and set Chat to Shown rather than Hidden.
Use the default Take Screenshot control, F2, or determine the currently assigned Take Screenshot key under Esc -> Options -> Controls if controls have been rebound.
Keep the game window focused and remain in normal gameplay with the HUD visible.

steps.action: From the Minecraft Launcher, start the installation/profile configured for Minecraft Java Edition 1.19.1 Pre-release 6. Do not substitute the listed fixed version, 1.19.1 Release Candidate 2.
steps.success_cue: The main menu displays Minecraft Java Edition 1.19.1 Pre-release 6 as the running version.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer and create a new world in Creative mode, or load another single-player world in which commands are permitted. If creating a world, wait for world generation and surrounding chunk loading to finish before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The player is in a loaded world, movement responds normally, and commands can be executed.

steps.action: Ensure normal chat display is enabled. If chat is hidden, press Esc, open Options, open Chat Settings, change the Chat setting to Shown, and return to the world.
steps.success_cue: The player has returned to gameplay with chat configured to display messages.

steps.action: Open the in-game chat/command entry field using the Open Chat control, which is T by default.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to accept text.

steps.action: Type the report's tag command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter to execute it as the current player.
steps.success_cue: A command feedback message appears in chat confirming execution, providing the report's system-message comparison line.

steps.action: Without leaving the world, press the Take Screenshot control once. The default key is F2; if that control has been rebound, press the key currently assigned to Take Screenshot instead.
steps.success_cue: A screenshot is saved and the screenshot feedback message has just been emitted into the in-game chat area.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just pressed Take Screenshot once in Minecraft Java Edition 1.19.1 Pre-release 6, after first producing the command-feedback comparison message with `/tag @s add test`. The screenshot feedback message is now present for immediate visual inspection by the observation subsystem.
uncertainties: The report does not specify single-player versus multiplayer, game mode, world seed, coordinates, or a particular world. This plan uses a new Creative single-player world as the minimum deterministic way to obtain command permission without adding server dependencies.
The report names F2 as the default Take Screenshot control but does not state whether controls were rebound; the executor should use the configured Take Screenshot binding if F2 is not assigned.
The report does not specify non-default chat settings, so the plan explicitly uses the Shown chat setting to ensure both comparison messages are visible.

source_meta._title: Chat messages can no longer be reported if the chat is enabled

stor.recommended_version: Minecraft: Java Edition 26.1 (the exact affected release)
stor.environment: Two concurrently running, unmodified Minecraft: Java Edition 26.1 clients, each signed in to a different authenticated account, connected to the same vanilla Java Edition 26.1 dedicated server configured with online-mode=true. Use English (US) UI text if exact menu-label matching is required.
preconditions: Designate Account A as the message sender and report target.
Designate Account B as the reporting account from which the Social Interactions and Report Player screens will be opened.
Both accounts must own Minecraft: Java Edition, be permitted to use online multiplayer, and be able to remain connected to the server simultaneously.
Account A and Account B must not be blocked through Microsoft/Xbox account-level social controls.
A vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition 26.1 server must be available to both clients, with the server.properties setting online-mode=true applied before server startup.
If the server uses a whitelist, both account usernames must already be permitted to join.
Do not use a proxy, plugin, mod, or server-side chat formatter that replaces or suppresses normal player chat messages.
Keep both players connected throughout the reproduction.
Do not submit a player report; the reproduction ends when the cursor is positioned over the Chat Messages button.

steps.action: Open the dedicated server's server.properties file and ensure online mode is enabled. Save the file before starting the server.
steps.success_cue: server.properties contains the saved line online-mode=true.

steps.action: Start the vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition 26.1 dedicated server using the reproduction environment's normal server-launch procedure. Do not continue until startup has completed.
steps.success_cue: The server is listening for connections and its console has reached the normal completed-startup state, typically indicated by a Done message.

steps.action: Launch two separate Minecraft: Java Edition clients. Sign the first client in as Account A and the second client in as Account B. Select the exact 26.1 installation on both clients rather than a snapshot, release candidate, or later release.
steps.success_cue: Both clients are at a title screen identifying the running game version as Minecraft: Java Edition 26.1, and each client displays the intended distinct account identity.

steps.action: From Account A's client, select Multiplayer, connect to the prepared online-mode server, and wait until the world and surrounding chunks have rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: Account A is present in the server world and can move normally.

steps.action: From Account B's client, connect to the same server and wait until the world and surrounding chunks have rendered and movement responds normally. Use the player-list control, Tab by default, to confirm both usernames are online.
steps.success_cue: The server player list contains both Account A and Account B, and Account B can move normally.

steps.action: On Account A's client, press Esc, select Options, open Chat Settings, and cycle the Chat setting until its value is Shown. Do not leave it on Commands Only or Hidden. Select Done as needed to return to gameplay.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options -> Chat Settings -> Chat: Shown
steps.success_cue: Account A is back in gameplay with the Chat setting showing Shown.

steps.action: On Account B's client, press Esc, select Options, open Chat Settings, and cycle the Chat setting until its value is Shown. This reporting client must not be set to Commands Only or Hidden. Select Done as needed to return to gameplay.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options -> Chat Settings -> Chat: Shown
steps.success_cue: Account B is back in gameplay with the Chat setting showing Shown.

steps.action: On Account A's client, press T to open normal player chat. Type the test message exactly as provided, then press Enter once to send it. Send it as ordinary player chat; do not use a command or the server console.
steps.success_cue: Account A's chat screen closes after sending, and the message appears in Account A's chat history under Account A's username.

steps.action: On Account B's client, wait for Account A's newly sent message to arrive. Do not change Account B's Chat setting after receiving it.
steps.success_cue: Account B's chat history visibly contains “MC-307140 reproduction message” attributed to Account A.

steps.action: On Account B's client, press Esc to open the multiplayer pause menu, then click Player Reporting to open the Social Interactions screen. The default P key may be used instead only if the pause-menu route is unavailable or the test harness is configured for keyboard navigation.
steps.success_cue: The Social Interactions player list is open and includes Account A's username.

steps.action: In Account B's Social Interactions player list, locate the row displaying Account A's username. Click Account A's Report Player button, identified by the reporting or yellow warning-symbol control rather than the hide-chat control.
steps.success_cue: The Report Player screen is open for Account A, and the Chat Messages button is visible on that screen.

steps.action: Without clicking the Chat Messages button, move Account B's mouse cursor onto the visible Chat Messages button and hold the cursor there. Do not alter the chat setting and do not proceed to submit a report.
steps.success_cue: The Report Player screen remains open for Account A, with the cursor stationary over the Chat Messages button.

stor.handoff_condition: Account B has just positioned the mouse cursor over the Chat Messages button on Account A's Report Player screen while both clients remain connected and Account B's Chat setting remains Shown. Hand control to the observation subsystem now.
uncertainties: The report specifies an online-mode server but does not state whether it was a dedicated server, Realm, or another deployment. This plan uses a vanilla dedicated server as the simplest deterministic online-mode environment.

The report does not explicitly identify which client's chat setting must be enabled. This plan sets Chat to Shown on both clients, ensuring Account A can send ordinary player chat and Account B can receive it under the reported condition.
The report does not provide server.properties values other than the online-mode requirement. Other server settings should remain at vanilla 26.1 defaults.
The exact icon appearance or wording for the Report Player control can vary with UI language and resource packs; the plan assumes the unmodified English (US) interface.
No message content was supplied by the report. The benign text “MC-307140 reproduction message” is a practical deterministic substitute.
